gap_analysis.objective: Compare LLM bidding in a one-round sealed-bid second-price auction (valuations 90/65/40) against the truthful-bidding reference.

requirement.description: One simultaneous sealed-bid round with exactly one scalar bid per bidder; no bidder observes another bid before committing.

decisions.reason: simultaneous.v1 runs all actors in one joint round before commitment, matching the sealed-bid timing; sealed privacy comes from per-actor observation permissions, not the protocol.

requirement.description: Three LLM bidder policies deciding from public rules plus their own private valuation only.

decisions.reason: llm.v1 supplies schema-constrained LLM decisions from observations with recorded rationales; scientific instructions, personas, and required fields are configured per bidder while the operator resolves transport.

requirement.description: Second-price allocation, payment, and utilities with configuration-order tie-break; strategically poor bids stay legal.

decisions.reason: No approved mechanism implements second-price rules: homogeneous_bertrand.v1 allocates to the lowest price, recording.v1 has no payoffs, and normal_form.v1 needs finite payoff tables. A Mechanism subclass implements the auction rules.

requirement.description: Scalar bid payload: one finite nonnegative number per bidder.

decisions.reason: A dedicated BidPayload gives the bid an explicit finite-nonnegative contract tied to the auction mechanism instead of reusing price-setting semantics.

requirement.description: Separately calculated truthful-bidding reference for benchmark comparison, computed after LLM decisions commit.

decisions.reason: The request asks for a separately calculated truthful strategy profile, not an equilibrium solver or completeness claim; a plain callable computing bids, winner, payment, and payoffs from valuations suffices.

requirement.description: Custom verification of allocation, payment, utilities, tie-break, and bid legality.

decisions.reason: Piecewise auction rules do not fit the numeric expression verification language; a VerificationCheck subclass recomputes allocation, payment, utilities, ties, and legality from the recorded run.

requirement.description: Explanatory final notebook plus offline preview through the shared report writers.

decisions.reason: The shared writers supply the five-section/preview structure; experiment-specific generator functions calculate the truthful benchmark, comparisons, and figures outside notebook cells.

components.purpose: Sealed-bid second-price auction rules: finite nonnegative bid legality, highest-bid-wins allocation with configuration-order tie-break, second-highest payment, quasi-linear utilities.

acceptance_tests.name: test_mechanism_clearing
acceptance_tests.expected: Bids 80/70/30 with valuations 90/65/40 clear winner bidder_a, payment 70.0, payoffs 20/0/0; bid history and outcome recorded in public state.
acceptance_tests.reference: Hand-derived second-price outcome: highest bid wins, pays second-highest, quasi-linear utility.

acceptance_tests.name: test_mechanism_tie_break
acceptance_tests.expected: Bids 60/60/40 select bidder_a by configuration order with payment 60.0 and payoff 30.0; all-zero bids select bidder_a with payment 0.0.
acceptance_tests.reference: Tie-break convention from the request; with tied top bids the second-highest submitted bid equals the top bid.

acceptance_tests.name: test_mechanism_overbidding_legal
acceptance_tests.expected: Bidder_b bidding 100 above valuation 65 is accepted, wins, pays 70 and receives utility -5.0.
acceptance_tests.reference: Request: overbidding is legal and negative utility is not a rejection reason.

acceptance_tests.name: test_mechanism_rejects_negative_bid
acceptance_tests.expected: A bid of -1.0 raises during action validation.
acceptance_tests.reference: Request: a bid is a finite nonnegative number.

acceptance_tests.name: test_mechanism_rejects_nonfinite_bid
acceptance_tests.expected: Infinite and NaN bids raise during action validation.
acceptance_tests.reference: Request: a bid is a finite nonnegative number.

acceptance_tests.name: test_mechanism_rejects_wrong_kind
acceptance_tests.expected: A wrong action kind or an incomplete bidder profile raises.
acceptance_tests.reference: One submit_bid action per bidder per round.

acceptance_tests.name: test_mechanism_rejects_unsupported_parameters
acceptance_tests.expected: Nonzero reserve, non-IPV value model, or fewer than two actors raise at config validation.
acceptance_tests.reference: Request fixes a no-reserve IPV auction; a second price needs at least two bids.

acceptance_tests.name: test_sealed_bid_run_offline
acceptance_tests.expected: Scripted offline run completes one round with the hand-derived outcome; each observation exposes only public rules plus the actor's own valuation.
acceptance_tests.reference: Runtime plus trusted observation projection; outcome hand-derived for the scripted bids.

components.purpose: Scalar bid payload carrying one finite nonnegative bid per bidder.

acceptance_tests.name: test_bid_payload_bounds
acceptance_tests.expected: Bids 0.0 and positive values validate; negative and nonfinite bids raise.
acceptance_tests.reference: Request: a bid is a finite nonnegative number.

components.purpose: Typed auction configuration: action/value/history/outcome field names plus fixed IPV, quasi-linear, no-reserve, no-budget, configuration-order settings.

acceptance_tests.name: test_auction_parameters_defaults
acceptance_tests.expected: Defaults validate to sealed second-price IPV settings; unsupported value model, utility model, reserve, budget, or tie-break values raise.
acceptance_tests.reference: Request assumptions: IPV, quasi-linear utility, no reserve, no budgets, configuration-order ties.

components.purpose: Plain callable computing the truthful-bidding reference (bids equal valuations, winner, payment, payoffs) from private valuations; not an equilibrium solver.

acceptance_tests.name: test_truthful_reference_main
acceptance_tests.expected: Valuations 90/65/40 give truthful bids, winner bidder_a, payment 65.0, payoffs 25/0/0.
acceptance_tests.reference: Hand-derived Vickrey outcome: highest value wins and pays the second-highest value.

acceptance_tests.name: test_truthful_reference_tie
acceptance_tests.expected: Valuations 50/50/30 give winner bidder_a by configuration order, payment 50.0, zero payoffs.
acceptance_tests.reference: Hand-derived Vickrey outcome plus the configuration-order tie-break convention.

acceptance_tests.name: test_truthful_weakly_dominant_sampled
acceptance_tests.expected: With rivals truthful at 65/40, bidder_a deviations across a grid never exceed the truthful payoff 25.0; sampled payoffs match hand-derived values.
acceptance_tests.reference: Textbook weak dominance of truthful bidding under IPV quasi-linear utility; grid payoffs hand-derived from the payment rule.

acceptance_tests.name: test_truthful_reference_rejects_single_bidder
acceptance_tests.reference: A second price is undefined without at least two bids.

components.purpose: VerificationCheck subclass recomputing allocation, payment, utilities, tie-break, and bid legality from the recorded run.

acceptance_tests.name: test_custom_check_verified
acceptance_tests.expected: Assessment of the recorded scripted run returns verified with allocation, payment, utility, tie-break, and legality evidence.
acceptance_tests.reference: Independent recomputation from committed actions and configured valuations.

acceptance_tests.name: test_custom_check_detects_tampering
acceptance_tests.reference: Independent recomputation from committed actions and configured valuations.

components.purpose: Offline (JobManifest, Path) -> Path preview generator explaining the problem, calculated truthful benchmark, assumptions, and limitations.

acceptance_tests.name: test_preview_notebook_pending
acceptance_tests.expected: Preview writes preview.ipynb from configuration only, leaving observed results and rationales pending.
acceptance_tests.reference: Notebook contract: offline preview without recorded decisions or performance interpretation.

components.purpose: Final (JobResult, Path) -> Path notebook generator comparing actual bids, winner, payment, and payoffs against the truthful reference with recorded rationales.

acceptance_tests.name: test_results_notebook_sections
acceptance_tests.expected: Report writes results.ipynb with five explanatory sections, the truthful reference comparison, and figures bound to the recorded result.
acceptance_tests.reference: Notebook contract: five sections derived from the saved run, calculations outside cells.

custom_checks.purpose: Recompute winner, payment, utilities, tie-break, and bid legality from committed actions and configured valuations; fail on any mismatch.
